title: Custom Tag Helpers
description: Create your own tag helpers to transform HTML elements, inject reusable styling, and encapsulate server-side logic in views.

data.text: When the built-in tag helpers are not enough, you can write your own. A custom tag helper is a C# class that derives from `TagHelper` and overrides the `Process` or `ProcessAsync` method. During view rendering, ASP.NET Core matches HTML elements to your tag helper, calls your code, and replaces or augments the element's output.

terms.definition: The base class for all tag helpers; provides Process() and ProcessAsync() to transform output.
An attribute that defines which elements your tag helper applies to.
Passed to Process(); provides metadata about the element being transformed.
Passed to Process(); represents the element's output that you can modify.
A method on TagHelperOutput that removes the element entirely from the rendered page.

data.text: Creating Your First Custom Tag Helper

A custom tag helper needs three things: a class that derives from `TagHelper`, an `[HtmlTargetElement]` attribute to declare which elements it applies to, and a `Process` method that modifies the output.

data.title: Naming convention
data.text: Property names use PascalCase in C# (BtnColor) but kebab-case in HTML (btn-color). ASP.NET Core converts between them automatically.
Controlling Scope with HtmlTargetElement

By default, a tag helper applies to any element that has the specified attribute. You can narrow the scope by combining multiple conditions in a single `[HtmlTargetElement]` attribute, or by stacking multiple attributes.

data.text: TagHelperOutput: Modifying the Element
The `TagHelperOutput` object is your main tool for transforming an element. It exposes properties for the tag name, attributes, and content, and methods for inserting content around the element.

rows: Get or set the tag name for the output element.
Dictionary of all attributes on the output element.
The inner content of the element.
HTML inserted before the element (outside the tag).
HTML inserted after the element (outside the tag).
Content inserted at the start of the element, before existing content.
Content inserted at the end of the element, after existing content.
Prevents the element from being rendered at all.

data.text: Coordinating Between Tag Helpers with TagHelperContext.Items
`TagHelperContext.Items` is a shared dictionary that lets parent and child tag helpers communicate. A parent tag helper can store a value, and any child tag helper inside it can read that value.

data.content: The parent stores a theme; child buttons read it automatically.

data.text: Accessing ViewContext

A tag helper can access the current `ViewContext` — which includes routing data, ViewBag, ViewData, and the current HTTP request — by declaring a property decorated with `[ViewContext]` and `[HtmlAttributeNotBound]`.

data.title: Reading the current route values inside a tag helper
data.content: Inject ViewContext to access routing data.

data.text: Suppressing Output
Call `output.SuppressOutput()` when you want to remove the element entirely from the rendered page. This is useful for conditional rendering without `if` statements in the view.

data.content: SuppressOutput removes the element from the rendered HTML.

data.text: Custom Tag Helpers for Custom HTML Elements

You can target non-standard HTML elements. If you use `<alert-box type="warning">...</alert-box>` in your view, a custom tag helper can transform it into a styled `<div>` — giving you fully custom, semantic markup.

data.title: Exercise: Build a reusable Card tag helper
data.description: Create a custom tag helper that transforms a custom <info-card> element into a Bootstrap card.
steps: Create a new C# class called InfoCardTagHelper in a CustomTagHelpers folder.
Add properties for Title (string) and Body (string).
In the Process method, set TagName to "div", add the Bootstrap card classes, and build the inner HTML with the title and body.
Use <info-card> in a view and verify it renders as a styled Bootstrap card.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Custom tag helpers are C# classes that derive from TagHelper.
HtmlTargetElement defines which HTML elements the helper applies to.
Process() modifies TagHelperOutput: tag name, attributes, content, and surrounding elements.
TagHelperContext.Items lets parent and child tag helpers share state.
ViewContext gives access to routing, ViewBag, and the current HTTP request.
SuppressOutput() removes the element from the rendered page entirely.
data.takeaway: Custom tag helpers turn repetitive view markup into clean, reusable, server-powered components. Use them whenever built-in helpers cannot express the HTML transformation you need.
